newsitem.title: USA: U.S. strikes at luxury car smuggling rings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. strikes at luxury car smuggling rings.

text.p: U.S. law enforcement officers Tuesday arrested four men accused of smuggling stolen luxury cars to Hong Kong and China, federal prosecutors said.

San Francisco residents Jimmy Dieu, 53; Kevin Gee, 40; Rowell Soriano, 22; and Darwin Soriano, 27, of American Canyon, Calif. were arrested in the early hours of Tuesday, the U.S. Attorney's office for northern California said.

A federal grand jury indicted the four men on April 22 on charges of conspiracy, export of stolen automobiles, removal of motor vehicle numbers and trafficking in motor vehicles with removed vehicle identification numbers.
A fifth defendant, Tommy Ng, 37, of San Francisco, was arrested earlier this month. He faces the same charges as well as numerous counts of money laundering, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
Dieu and Gee own auto body repair businesses in the San Francisco area while Ng owns an auto trading concern, it said.

The newly-unsealed indictment alleges the defendants stole late model luxury automobiles in northern California, replaced their vehicle identification numbers with numbers from junked salvage vehicles bought at auction, and shipped them to Hong Kong and China.
The indictment said 12 cars had been exported or were in the process of being exported by the stolen car ring.
The men could face up to 10 years in prison for each stolen vehicle, Assistant U.S. Attorney William Schaefer said.

He said vehicle smuggling was a major problem in California and fighting it was a priority of federal prosecutors. "They are almost exclusively the high-end, luxury cars because they can sell for large amounts of money overseas," he said.
The arrests stemmed from a joint investigation by the U.S. Customs Service, the Internal Revenue Service and the California Highway Patrol.
The U.S. Attorney's office also said two people were indicted by a federal grand jury Tuesday over their alleged involvement in a separate stolen automobile export ring.

Guilliano Pacino, 31, of Los Angeles and Youssef Alami, 29, who is from Morocco, were indicted on 15 counts of conspiracy, export of stolen motor vehicles, transport of stolen vehicles and removal of motor vehicles.
Each count carries a maximum sentence of either five or 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
The indictment alleges the two men stole late model luxury automobiles from southern California and shipped them to the Netherlands and Germany.

Pacino and Alami were arrested on March 28 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, while attempting to pick up a stolen car shipped from Oakland, California, the U.S. Attorney's office said. The United States has asked the Netherlands to extradite them back to California for prosecution, it said.
